blocks.text: Requirements are generally categorized into two types: functional and non-functional requirements.

blocks.title: Functional requirements
blocks.text: Functional requirements describe the specific behaviours or functions of a system: what the system should do, including the tasks, services and functions it must perform and its interactions with users or other systems.

items: User registration: users (students, faculty) can register and create an account.
Book borrowing: users can search for books and borrow them.
Book return: users can return borrowed books.
Inventory management: librarians can add, update and remove books.
Notification: the system sends notices about due dates and overdue books.

blocks.title: Non-functional requirements
blocks.text: Non-functional requirements define the quality attributes, performance criteria and constraints of the system. They specify how the system performs a function rather than what it does, covering usability, reliability, performance and security.

items: Performance: handle up to 1000 simultaneous users without slowing down.
Usability: an intuitive interface that is easy to navigate.
Security: encrypted user data and secure authentication.
Scalability: grow to more users and more books.
